The listings import `@preview/keisen:0.1.0`, which is how they will read once the package is released.
There is no release yet, so a reader trying them today imports `lib.typ` from a clone instead.

Every table in this section is rendered from a file in the repository's `tests/visual/` directory, and each image is that file's own output, regenerated by `tools/render-docs-assets.sh`.
The listings are the test sources, quoted; `tools/check.sh` compiles those tests on every run and `tools/dry-release.sh` compiles the listings themselves against an installed copy of the package.

## A table, built and formatted

The smallest thing worth calling a display table: a title, labelled columns, formatted numbers, and a source note.

```typst
#import "@preview/keisen:0.1.0": *

#display-table(
  (
    model: ("Audi A4", "BMW 320i", "Volkswagen Golf"),
    consumption: (7.25, 8.5, 6.125),
    year: (2019, 2021, 2020),
  ),
  table-header(
    title: [Fuel consumption],
    subtitle: [Litres per 100 kilometres],
  ),
  columns-label(model: [Model], consumption: [Consumption], year: [Year]),
  format-number("consumption", decimals: 2),
  format-integer("year", grouping: none),
  table-source-note([Source: manufacturer figures.]),
)
```

![A table titled Fuel consumption with three car models, their consumption to two decimals, and the model year, above a source note.](../assets/examples/minimal.png)

Numeric columns align themselves against the end edge and the others against the start edge, so nothing needed saying about alignment.
`6.125` rounds to `6.13`: the default is half-up, computed in decimal arithmetic rather than in floats.

That is the shape of every table below.
Data goes in first, directives follow in the order they should apply, and the theme is an argument like any other.

## Find your case

- [Total a table by group](total-by-group.qmd), with a subtotal closing each block and a grand total closing the table.
- [Draw attention to a total](highlight-a-total.qmd), by shading a subtotal row and marking it with a note.
- [Group rows the data does not group](declare-your-own-groups.qmd), when no column says which rows belong together.
- [Report an estimate with its error](estimate-with-its-error.qmd), reading two columns as one.
- [Write values in their own notation](values-in-their-own-notation.qmd): money, magnitudes, sizes, dates, and markup.
- [Write numbers the local way](numbers-the-local-way.qmd), setting the separators once for the whole table.
- [Mark a cell that fails a threshold](mark-a-failing-cell.qmd), styled by what the data says rather than by where the cell sits.
- [Carry a table across pages](table-across-pages.qmd), with the labels and the group reprinted overleaf.
- [Show a trend inside a cell](trend-inside-a-cell.qmd), on one scale down the column.
- [Set a plot in a sentence](plot-in-a-sentence.qmd), at the height of the text around it.
- [Set a table right to left](right-to-left.qmd), mirrored with the writing direction.
